rationale:
ROUND 3 — revising on round 2's REVISE (gating objection from reuse_agent). Every objection below was acted on in CODE, and two of them found real defects in what round 2 shipped.

GATING (reuse_agent, HIGH) — 'the plan writes a brand-new parallel function resolveLogoIntent instead of extending resolveKind/kindDefaults… two kind-resolution functions now coexist in one action for the same axis, in the same file the diagnosis already cites.' Correct, and embarrassing given the diagnosis: I objected to a rule attached to the wrong signal and then added a second resolver beside the existing one rather than fixing it.
FIXED: resolveLogoIntent is DELETED. resolveKind is now the one resolver, extended with the extra sources and returning an `imageKind{Kind, Signal, Answered, Conflict}` instead of a bare string — because a string cannot express the two things the other objections turned on.

bug_historian (MEDIUM) — 'believing any stated non-logo kind opens the mirror case: a caller that mislabels a logo with a WRONG non-empty kind silently skips the policy, with no Warn, no note, no error surface — reproducing 417 on a THIRD axis, and this one gets none of the round-2 detection built for the other two.' Right, and it is the same shape twice over.
FIXED: resolveKind now compares a STATED kind against the step's own name and records a `Conflict` when they disagree; the caller files an `image_kind_conflict` row. The stated kind still WINS — a classifier overriding a caller is a worse failure than a recorded disagreement — but a mislabelled logo is now findable instead of silently ungoverned. This is two declarations disagreeing, deterministically; no classifier is inferring anything.

editquality (MEDIUM) — 'resolveLogoIntent returns (false, "") in TWO distinct situations the caller cannot tell apart… the residual detector fires on kind == "" alone, so a hero/icon call that sets purpose but never sets kind files a FALSE image_generation_without_kind note. That pollutes exactly the liveness measurement this round claims to have fixed.' Right — my compensating control would have been noisy in precisely the way that made it useless.
FIXED: `Answered` reports whether ANY source identified the generation, even as a non-logo, and the detector gates on `!Answered`, which is the question that was actually meant. Pinned by a test case that sets purpose without kind.

editquality (LOW) — 'the step.Config branch in the sketch is a bare comment stub… as presented this signal is not implemented.' Fair on the sketch; it WAS implemented. Round 3's sketch shows the real body.

tooling_provenance (MEDIUM) + constitution (LOW) + guardian (LOW) — the hand-rolled doc_notes INSERT. THIS OBJECTION FOUND A LIVE BUG, and it is the most valuable thing in the round. The guardian's phrasing was the sharpest: a constraint mismatch 'WOULD silently null out the exact detector round 2 leans on as its liveness measurement.' Verified against the live schema [MEASURED 2026-08-31]: `doc_notes_subject_type_check` permits exactly eight values — tool, pipeline, experience, action, experience-pattern, landmine, component, decision — and round 2's insert used `subject_type='site'`. **Every insert would have failed**, and because the writer was best-effort it would have failed SILENTLY. The compensating control was broken on arrival.
FIXED, and fixed by reuse rather than by patching the literal (reuse_agent MEDIUM: 'no rationale shows the existing durable-recording family was checked'). recordImagePolicyEvent now calls LogActionEntryInheritingProvenance / agenterrors.Entry — the estate's action-level recording family, which carries SiteID/AgentType/StepName/Action/ErrorCode/Severity/Context and is best-effort by construction. A reused writer cannot get its own table's constraints wrong, which is the general lesson: the hand-rolled insert failed for a reason the reuse objection would have prevented without anyone noticing the constraint at all.

guardian (MEDIUM) — 'the step_name arm needs the live step-name population ENUMERATED, not asserted.' Done, and it changed the code. `[MEASURED 2026-08-31]` every live step name containing 'logo' or 'hero' across all active agent definitions: call_logo_gen, call_logo_generation, generate_logo, store_logo_asset, deploy_logo_image, check_logo_or_hero. **check_logo_or_hero names BOTH kinds** — so stepNameKindHint now returns NO hint when a name contains both (or neither) rather than guessing, and that case is pinned by test against the real live name. The enumeration is in the function's comment so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.

guardian (MEDIUM) — 'the plan does not confirm applyLogoTextPolicy's 3→4 return widening has only one call site.' Confirmed by grep [MEASURED 2026-08-31]: exactly ONE non-test call site (generate_image_actions.go, in GenerateImageAction). The package builds and the full suite is green, which is the stronger check.

prior_art_librarian (MEDIUM) — 'the RFC_022 scope hinges on constraints.wordmark_text having ZERO occurrences, asserted as MEASURED but quoted in prose.' Re-run, and the honest answer has CHANGED: the string now appears 3× in generate_image_actions.go, because round 2's code is in the tree. The claim must therefore be stated with its baseline — **zero occurrences BEFORE this change** — and the RFC_022 classification rests on that plus the two conditions that are properties of the design (opt-in; unsafe side OFF), which are unchanged. There is now also one live DATA consumer (farmerinsurance.uk's plan row), disclosed in round 2.

debug_historian (MEDIUM) — 'the risk section says to verify the roll at the build provenance stamp; the platform's own landmine calls that unreliable.' Right, and it matters because this fix is inert until the roll, so a wrong verification method means believing the guard is live while the pre-fix binary is running. The risks section now prescribes a pod-grep of the RUNNING binary for this change's own literals, with a present-and-absent control pair.

reuse_agent / prior_art (LOW) — loadLogoIdentity vs default_brand_prompt.go's loadSiteBrandFacts. Not merged, deliberately, and the reason is in the code: loadLogoIdentity reads `logo_text`, which loadSiteBrandFacts does not, and it must NOT inherit that loader's identity-spec reads — whose own header says 'Do NOT add a long key-guessing ladder here'. Pulling a validation lookup through a prompt-composition loader would couple a correctness check to a deliberately lossy helper. Stated rather than silently ignored.

architecture (LOW, on an APPROVE) — accepted as written: step-name matching is a heuristic on a shared choke point, and if it needs repeated extension for new caller shapes it has become an accumulating special-case surface rather than a contract. The new image_generation_without_kind detector is the trigger to revisit: if it fires often, the answer is to fix the callers' input_mapping, not to add arms here.

--- ROUND 2 RATIONALE, unchanged below ---

ROUND 2 — revising on round 1's REVISE (gating objection from bug_historian, corr bb099a3d-0555-4fcf-b12a-31652b59f8b9). Both objections were correct and BOTH ARE NOW CLOSED IN CODE, not answered in prose.

OBJECTION 1 (HIGH) — 'keying the guard on `kind` alone reproduces bug 417's own root cause on a second axis instead of closing it; disclosing the gap in risks does not close the exposure.' That is right, and it is the sharpest possible statement of what was wrong with round 1: the whole thesis of this change is that a policy attached to the wrong signal governs only the population that never needed it — and I then attached the new policy to a signal two live parents do not supply, and wrote it up as a risk. A risks block is not a control.
FIXED: the trigger is no longer `kind == "logo"`. `resolveLogoIntent` resolves the intent from every signal the action has — `kind`, `input_data.purpose`, `input_data.spec.purpose`, the step config's `purpose` and `kind`, and finally the STEP NAME, which is the one signal the two legacy parents do carry (their step is literally `call_logo_generation`). The signal that answered is appended to `prompt_source` (`+via_step_name`), so the artefact records not just that the policy fired but WHY it fired. A positively-stated non-logo `kind` short-circuits to false first, which is what keeps hero/icon/imagery prompts out of the logo policy — the 2026-05-20 contamination lesson's mirror, and pinned by test.
AND THE RESIDUAL IS NOW DETECTED RATHER THAN DOCUMENTED: if nothing identifies the generation at all, the action files a durable `image_generation_without_kind` note naming the agent, the step and the prompt source. That converts an undetectable silence into a row — and it doubles as the measurement I told round 1 I could not obtain. My `orchestration_states` liveness probe for those parents returned zero, and returned zero for a known-live control too, so it settled nothing. This detector settles it: if those parents are dead the table stays empty, and that empty is the answer; if they are alive, every row names the run that got through.

OBJECTION 2 (MEDIUM) — 'on rejection the guard only logs a Warn; no durable record, matching bugs_open/034's validation-errors-dropped pattern.' Also right, and it matters more than it looks because the rejection path is the one place a planner LLM's behaviour becomes visible.
FIXED: `applyLogoTextPolicy` now returns the rejected string as a fourth value, and the caller files a durable `logo_wordmark_rejected` note carrying the requested text and the site's actual naming. A census can now ask 'is something repeatedly proposing ungrounded wordmarks?' without reading logs. Note insertion is best-effort so it can never fail a generation, but a note failure is logged loudly — a silent note failure would recreate exactly the invisibility this removes.

editquality's two LOW objections, answered: (a) the helper bodies were not in the sketch — they are in this round's edit 2 sketch, and `params.DB`/`siteID` are both in scope at the call site (the same `siteID` the direction block above it uses, and the same `params.DB` the store path uses); the identity lookup is also only performed when someone opts IN, so the default path takes no query. (b) the clause asserts to the model that the brand name is set in HTML beside the logo — accepted as imprecise: chrome currently suppresses the visible name when a logo image exists (alt text only), so the clause states an intent the chrome does not yet guarantee. It is left as written because it is the instruction we want the model to follow, and the chrome gap is recorded in bugs_open/417 §8 as a design-family follow-up rather than silently implied to be solved.

A LIVE CONSUMER APPEARED SINCE ROUND 1, and the reviewer should hear it from me: the loanzy lane set `constraints.wordmark_text = "farmerinsurance"` on farmerinsurance.uk's current plan row (b6680524), giving the owner's named exception a durable home. Round 1's RFC_022 third-condition claim was '0 occurrences in platform/ internal/ pkg/ cmd/' — that was scoped to the REPO and remains true, since this is a data row rather than code, and the field is still opt-in with the unsafe side OFF. So the scope judgement is unchanged. But the plain reading of 'zero live consumers' is now stale, and it exposed a NEAR-MISS worth recording: that site's `company_name` and `logo_text` are BOTH EMPTY, so the ask grounds only via the domain stem. Had I validated against the naming columns alone — the obvious reading of 'check it is this site's own name' — the owner's explicit instruction would have been REJECTED and silently degraded, on the one site where he asked for lettering. Pinned as a named test; deleting the domain-stem source alone breaks it.

--- ROUND 1 RATIONALE, unchanged below ---

bugs_open/417. The estate has a craft rule for generated logo marks — no lettering, because image models reliably malform text and this asset is re-derived into a favicon and an og_card — but the rule is attached to the wrong thing. It lives inside composeBrandImagePrompt in discovery_checks/default_brand_prompt.go, the FALLBACK builder, which runs only when a site plan supplies no logo prompt at all (load_work_item_actions.go:2391-2399 and check_placeholder_image_in_use.go:120-145 both call it only under `if prompt == ""`). Every planner-built site supplies a prompt, so the rule protects exactly the population that never needed it and the planned prompt reaches the image model ungoverned. The rule is coupled to the prompt's SOURCE rather than to the asset's PURPOSE.

The harm is live and owner-visible on two sites. build-site-planner's worked example said 'no text outside the wordmark itself' — a phrase that presupposes a wordmark, permits lettering inside it, and never says what it should read, so the model must invent the words. It produced 'Farm Shield Info' on farmerinsurance.uk and 'BOXING NEWS' on boxingonline.com, a site called Boxing Online and the FIRST PAID CUSTOMER, served in the header of 19 pages with the favicon and og_card derived from the same asset.

Migrations 669 (fix the exemplar) and 670 (wash the propagated prompts) shipped this morning with an APPROVED r1 verdict, and the same day proved them a FLOOR rather than a bound, in two measured ways. (1) THE RACE TAIL: site_plan_imagery b56182fa was created 2026-08-31 12:36:55Z, 41 seconds after 669 applied at 12:36:14Z, by a planner run already in flight; its asset was generated from it at 12:56:10Z. A migration that fixes a prompt SOURCE cannot bound prompts already in flight. (2) THE PARAPHRASE: that row reads 'no text OTHER THAN the wordmark itself' where the exemplar said 'OUTSIDE'. 670's surgical arm keyed on the literal and could never have matched it. The model rewords the licence, so no literal match bounds the class — and any post-fix census keyed on a literal measures its own literal.

This moves the rule to the one place every prompt from every tier and every producer must pass. getImagePromptWithPriority (generate_image_actions.go:395) has already collapsed step config, collected data, input_data, the agent's own prompt_template and the workflow fallback into one value; the bugs_open/210 refusal twenty lines below is the precedent that this function enforces policy; and the kind-gated direction block at :432-491 shows `kind` is already in hand and already used for logo-specific decisions. Applying the rule HERE, not at plan time, also governs work items ALREADY QUEUED with an unwashed prompt — which is precisely what 669/670 structurally could not do. The guard needs no detection of the licence at all, which is why it is a bound and not a floor.

MEASURED, not asked of the reviewer. The claim that a negative prompt would have been enough is FALSE and I have the adapter log for the failing generation: at 12:55:50Z the banana provider logged 'folded NegativePrompt into positive prompt as a prohibition clause', kind=logo, negative list including 'text', prompt_len 232->407. The model RECEIVED the text prohibition and lettered 'BOXING NEWS' anyway, because the positive prompt licensed a wordmark. A folded prohibition loses to a positive licence in the same prompt. So the rule must be a positive instruction that explicitly voids the earlier wording; the negative channel is belt only. This also corrects an assumption the old clause rested on — it was negative-framed, and therefore weaker than its own comment claimed, for as long as it stood.

The opt-in field is required, not polish: a concept census of all 28 current-plan logo prompts [MEASURED 2026-08-31] found ~8 that name their exact wordmark ON PURPOSE (cv1 'CareerPrep', idea.uk, oufe, relojistas, robot-hands, webdesign.uk, lendzy, loanzy), and the owner has separately instructed that farmerinsurance.uk's logo carry the exact wordmark 'farmerinsurance'. An unconditional text-free clause would wreck those on regeneration. Per the OWNER RULING of 2026-08-31 (logos carry no words by default; a lettered logo is allowed only where the exact string is named) and the 2026-08-02 ruling on new authority on a shared seam, this ships as an opt-in field whose UNSAFE side is OFF by default. The field's VALUE is the exact string, so 'a wordmark' with no text named — the 417 licence itself — is not expressible. The value is validated against the site's own company_name / logo_text / domain stem, and a mismatch DEGRADES to text-free with a Warn rather than refusing (the 210 unhandleable-item lesson). That grounding check is what closes the door against the field's own producer: a planner LLM can write this field, so 'the field exists' cannot be the licence — 'the field names THIS site' is.

RFC_022 scope check, enumerated rather than asserted: constraints.wordmark_text has ZERO occurrences in the repo before this change [MEASURED 2026-08-31, grep over platform/ internal/ pkg/ cmd/]; it is opt-in; its unsafe side is the default OFF. All three conditions hold, so this is normal council scope, not architecture scope. The optional-key budget (WFA-013, N=10) is not implicated: it counts RegisterActionInputSpec Optional keys, and this rides the EXISTING input_data.spec.constraints map whose unknown keys the Phase 2H block at :267-291 already ignores — so the key was inert on every path until this guard shipped.

Consumers named and told, per the 2026-07-29 ruling: the loanzy lane (filed 417, shipped 669/670, has formally handed me the residual), the boxingonline.com session (its site is the live instance and its regeneration must land after this), the site_delivery_and_editor lane (holds that site's delivery chain), and the vigilant_designer lane (declined fix candidate 2 on record). Migration 680, already applied, is the pre-roll protection for the one race-tail row, because this Go half is inert until the next chassis roll.

plan.summary: Move the estate's ruled logo text policy from the fallback prompt builder (where only promptless plans reach it) to GenerateImageAction's choke point, where every logo prompt from every producer passes — as an unconditional positive-framed governing clause, with a validated opt-in field for deliberately lettered marks whose value IS the exact string, so an unnamed wordmark becomes inexpressible.

edits.rationale: Single-source the policy as exported constants so the fallback path and the choke point cannot drift — the drift IS the bug, in the other direction. LogoTextFreeClause is positive-framed and explicitly overrides earlier wording, because the measured adapter log proves a folded negative loses to a positive licence in the same prompt. LogoTextFreeSentinel is kept separate as the idempotence key and the census needle, so rewording the clause cannot silently break idempotence on prompts already carrying it. LogoWordmarkClause takes the exact string. The logo branch keeps its form constraints and now ends with the shared constant instead of its own sentence.

ROUND 3. resolveLogoIntent is DELETED and resolveKind — the file's existing resolver for this exact axis — is extended instead (the gating reuse objection). It returns imageKind{Kind, Signal, Answered, Conflict}: Signal so the artefact records WHICH source let the policy fire; Answered so 'identified as non-logo' and 'nothing identified it' are distinguishable, which is what stops the residual detector false-positiving on a hero call that sets purpose but no kind; Conflict so a stated kind contradicted by the step's own name is recorded rather than silently skipping the policy. stepNameKindHint abstains on an ambiguous name — check_logo_or_hero is a real live step name containing both kinds. recordImagePolicyEvent now reuses LogActionEntryInheritingProvenance/agenterrors.Entry instead of a hand-rolled doc_notes INSERT, which also fixes a live bug: round 2's insert used subject_type='site', not one of the eight values the CHECK constraint permits, so it would have failed silently on every call and nulled out this round's own compensating control.

Tests the pure half against every shape that matters, using the REAL boxingonline prompt as the default fixture — the paraphrase 670 could not match. Header lists six mutations; each was applied ALONE and broke its named test (run 2026-08-31): restoring the defect, deleting the append, dropping idempotence, dropping negative reconciliation, accepting any string, breaking the normaliser. The grounding table pins case/punctuation folding, domain stems including multi-label suffixes (cv1.co.uk), and that a SUBSTRING is not a match. ROUND 2 adds TestResolveLogoIntentClosesTheLegacyParentGap (10 cases, incl. the legacy parents' step-name-only shape, 'nothing identifies it must NOT guess', and hero/icon being believed) and the owner's live farmerinsurance exception, which grounds ONLY on the domain stem because that site's company_name and logo_text are both empty. Four further mutations run alone, each breaking its named test: drop the step_name arm; default to logo when nothing identifies it; drop the stated-kind early return; stop surfacing the rejected wordmark. ROUND 3 replaces the resolver test with TestResolveKindClosesTheLegacyParentGapAndSurfacesDisagreement (12 cases over the merged resolveKind), pinning: every signal source; the legacy parents' step-name-only shape; the REAL live ambiguous name check_logo_or_hero abstaining; 'nothing identified it' as distinct from 'identified as non-logo'; and a mislabelled logo being BELIEVED but flagged. Four mutations run alone, each breaking it: delete the step_name arm; drop the Conflict assignment; set Answered unconditionally; make the ambiguous name guess.

Makes the single-sourcing load-bearing: pins that the fallback logo prompt still carries LogoTextFreeClause VERBATIM, that a hero prompt does NOT carry it (the mirror of the 2026-05-20 contamination lesson — heroes legitimately have overlaid headline text), and that LogoWordmarkClause quotes the exact string. Mutation: replacing the shared constant at either site with a fresh literal saying the same thing — run 2026-08-31, breaks the parity test.

APPLIED 2026-08-31 (rehearsed with ROLLBACK first: exactly 1 row). Pre-roll protection for the single race-tail row, since the Go guard is inert until the next chassis build. Follows 670 arm (b): an appended dated governing clause, idempotence-guarded, leaving the original wording auditable. DELIBERATELY omits a widened regex safety-net arm: the concept census found exactly one licence-without-name row and ~8 rows that name their wordmark on purpose, and a regex broad enough to catch a paraphrase is broad enough to void a deliberate worded mark, silently. Verified after: 0 wordmark-mentioning current logo prompts lack a governing clause.

CONFIRMED against the live schema [MEASURED 2026-08-31]: doc_notes_subject_type_check permits only tool, pipeline, experience, action, experience-pattern, landmine, component, decision — round 2 used 'site'.

plan.risks:
The Go half is INERT until the next chassis build and roll.

ROLL VERIFICATION — corrected in round 3 on the debug_historian objection. Do NOT verify this by the 'build provenance' log line: the platform's own landmine record says that grep matches NOTHING on a backend service and, on agent-chassis specifically, can match ANOTHER LANE'S PAYLOAD. Verify at the RUNNING BINARY, with a control pair: `kubectl -n ai-persona-system exec <pod> -- grep -aq 'image_kind_conflict' /proc/1/exe` must SUCCEED after the roll, and a literal that cannot be present must FAIL in the same breath. Never `strings` (absent from the debian-slim images). This matters more than usual because the fix is inert until the roll and the whole residual argument leans on it being live.

Clause OBEDIENCE is [ASSUMED] until a canary. What is MEASURED is only that a positive licence beat a folded negative on the failing generation. Run 5+ generations per bugs_closed/028 §6, download the PNGs and look. Clause present in origin_prompt but lettering still in the image is a prompt-engineering failure, distinct from the guard not firing — only the origin_prompt mark and the +via_<signal> tag separate them.

THE RESIDUAL, after three rounds, stated precisely: a caller that supplies no kind, no default_kind, no purpose, no step-config kind/purpose AND whose step name names neither 'logo' nor 'hero' is still ungoverned. That case now files image_generation_without_kind rather than passing silently, so it is bounded by observation. A caller that MISLABELS its kind is still obeyed — deliberately, since a classifier overriding a caller is the worse failure — but now files image_kind_conflict. Both are detections, not preventions, and they are honestly labelled as such.

The step-name arm is a heuristic on a shared choke point and the architecture seat's LOW is accepted: if it needs repeated extension for new caller shapes it has become an accumulating special-case surface rather than a contract. The image_generation_without_kind detector is the trigger to revisit — and the right response to it firing often is to fix the callers' input_mapping, not to add arms here. Its false-positive cost is bounded: appending a text-free clause to a non-logo prompt AGREES with the estate's own hero rule, which already says 'no embedded words or lettering'.

The two new recording codes are new rows on a path that had none. If the legacy parents turn out to be live and busy, image_generation_without_kind could be chatty; that volume is itself the finding, and the honest response is to fix the callers, not silence the record.

The post-fix census must key on the CONCEPT and on the policy's own tag/sentinel, never on the licence literal — the model rewords it, which is the whole finding.

The 'brand name is set in HTML beside the logo' half of the contract is NOT currently guaranteed: chrome suppresses the visible name when a logo image exists (alt text only). Recorded in bugs_open/417 §8 as a design-family follow-up; the clause states the intent we want the model to follow and the gap is not silently implied to be solved.

loadLogoIdentity is deliberately NOT merged into default_brand_prompt.go's loadSiteBrandFacts: it reads logo_text, which that loader does not, and must not inherit its identity-spec reads (whose own header says 'Do NOT add a long key-guessing ladder here'). Coupling a correctness check to a deliberately lossy prompt-composition helper would be the wrong reuse.
